notes: Commercial-but-open model: hardware is sold but the design is published openly.

disclosure_citation: Skuric, Antun et al. SimpleFOC library release, 2020.
creator: SimpleFOC community
actuator_details: Open Arduino-compatible FOC library for BLDC and stepper motors
prior_art_notes: SimpleFOC is significant prior art for educational/open FOC implementations. Has lowered the barrier to entry for hobbyist robotics actuator development.
notes: Less performance-oriented than ODrive/Moteus but enormously broad in adoption.

disclosure_citation: Boston Dynamics partnership announcements with fuel cell vendors, 2020.
creator: Boston Dynamics
ip_citations: Boston Dynamics patents on Spot platform
prior_art_notes: Demonstrates fuel-cell-powered legged robotics at commercial scale. Anticipates fuel-cell power claims in field robotics applications.
notes: Variant entry rather than full Spot lineage; covers the power-fuel-cell taxonomy gap.

disclosure_citation: Unitree Robotics G1 reveal, May 2024.
creator: Unitree Robotics
actuator_details: Custom electric actuators including cycloidal reducers in some joints
ip_citations: Unitree patent filings primarily in PRC
prior_art_notes: G1's actuator IP largely anticipated by MIT Mini Cheetah QDD work and Honda harmonic drive prior art. The aggressive pricing represents the commodity-humanoid trajectory more than novel IP.
notes: G1 cycloidal reducers fill that taxonomy gap; sub-$20K pricing is the market-moving feature.

disclosure_citation: Ha, I. et al. 'Development of Open Humanoid Platform DARwIn-OP.' SICE 2011.
creator: Robotis Co. with University of Pennsylvania, Virginia Tech, Purdue
control_architecture: open behavior tree and walk pattern generators
prior_art_notes: DARwIn-OP is foundational prior art for fully-open small-scale humanoid platforms. Predates Poppy by several years for the academic-open category.
notes: Major influence on the educational/research humanoid space.

disclosure_citation: Gouaillier, D. et al. 'Mechatronic design of NAO humanoid.' ICRA 2009.
creator: Aldebaran Robotics (later SoftBank Robotics, then UBT)
actuator_details: Custom electric actuators with brushed and brushless motors
control_architecture: NAOqi middleware; behavior trees and learned components

disclosure_citation: SoftBank Robotics public reveal of Pepper, June 2014.
creator: SoftBank Robotics (formerly Aldebaran)
sensing: cameras, microphones, IMU, lasers, sonars, tactile
prior_art_notes: Pepper is foundational prior art for wheeled-base humanoid social robots. The omnidirectional wheeled base design has been widely cited.
notes: Production officially ended in 2021 but units remain widely deployed.

disclosure_citation: Willow Garage. PR2 platform release, 2010.
creator: Willow Garage
actuator_details: Custom electric actuators with series-elastic in some joints
control_architecture: ROS-based (PR2 was a primary driver of ROS development)
sensing: stereo cameras, LiDAR, force-torque, tilting laser
ip_citations: Willow Garage open release; ROS BSD license
prior_art_notes: PR2 was the platform around which ROS was originally built. Its hardware is significant prior art for omnidirectional wheeled mobile manipulation. ROS itself is even more significant prior art for robotics middleware.
sources: Quigley, M. et al. 'ROS: an open-source Robot Operating System.' ICRA Workshop 2009.
notes: Willow Garage is defunct but PR2's influence persists through ROS, MoveIt, and the broad community. Several PR2 units remain in academic operation.

disclosure_citation: Black, K. et al. 'π0: A Vision-Language-Action Flow Model for General Robot Control.' arXiv 2410.24164, October 2024.
creator: Physical Intelligence
control_architecture: VLA model with flow-matching policy head
ip_citations: arXiv preprint discloses architecture; weights and dataset proprietary
prior_art_notes: π0 paper discloses VLA-with-flow-matching architecture publicly. The arXiv preprint is itself prior art for that specific architectural pattern.
notes: Software/policy entry rather than embodiment entry; exists across many platforms.

disclosure_citation: Sha, Lui. 'Dependable system upgrade.' Proceedings 19th IEEE Real-Time Systems Symposium, 1998. Earlier conceptual work circa 1995.
creator: Lui Sha, Carnegie Mellon University
control_architecture: Simplex: high-assurance simple controller with verified safety envelope, alongside complex high-performance controller, with a decision module that switches to the simple controller when complex controller violates envelope
notable_capabilities: formal safety guarantees in presence of complex/unverified control
backbone of much modern safety-critical control
ip_citations: academic publication; concept widely adopted without IP enforcement
prior_art_notes: Foundational prior art for safety supervisor architectures in robotics and physical AI. Any 'safety supervisor' or 'safety envelope' or 'fallback controller' patent claim post-1995 must contend with Sha's Simplex work as anticipating prior art. Directly relevant to MathGround's Simplex supervisor architecture.
sources: Sha, L. 'Using Simplicity to Control Complexity.' IEEE Software 18(4), 2001.
Crenshaw, T.L. et al. 'The Simplex reference model: limiting fault-propagation due to unreliable components in cyber-physical system architectures.' RTSS 2007.
notes: Simplex is among the most-cited safety architecture concepts in real-time and cyber-physical systems literature.

disclosure_citation: Schierman, J.D. et al. 'Runtime Assurance Framework Development for Highly Adaptive Flight Control Systems.' Air Force Research Laboratory, 2015. Earlier DARPA AACUS work circa 2010.
creator: Air Force Research Laboratory and DARPA program
control_architecture: Runtime monitor that switches between primary and verified backup controller based on safety constraint satisfaction
notable_capabilities: enables fielding of unverified ML-based controllers in safety-critical aviation
ip_citations: AFRL technical reports; DARPA-funded; broadly published
prior_art_notes: Direct descendant of Simplex; the 'unverified neural net plus verified safety controller' pattern. Anticipates modern ML-safety supervisor patents in autonomous vehicles, drones, and robotics. Directly applicable as prior art to safety claims in physical AI products.
notes: AFRL RTA work is widely cited but underappreciated outside aerospace. Worth surfacing in robotics-domain prior art arguments.

disclosure_citation: Wieland, P. and Allgöwer, F. 'Constructive safety using control barrier functions.' IFAC Proceedings Volumes 40(12), 2007.
creator: Peter Wieland and Frank Allgöwer (early formalization); Aaron Ames and others (modern formalization)
control_architecture: Lyapunov-like functions that certify forward invariance of a safe set under a control law; can be composed with QP-based controllers for online safety filtering
notable_capabilities: composable with arbitrary nominal controllers via QP
applied across robotics, vehicles, multi-agent systems
prior_art_notes: CBFs are the dominant modern formalism for online safety filtering in robotics. Substantial prior art for any patent claiming online safety filtering, safety-aware QP control, or formally-bounded safe ML execution. Particularly relevant to MathGround's Universal Fuzz Law work as the formal foundation for safety envelopes.
sources: Wieland, P. and Allgöwer, F. IFAC 2007.
Ames, A.D. et al. 'Control Barrier Function Based Quadratic Programs for Safety Critical Systems.' IEEE TAC 62(8), 2017.
Ames, A.D. et al. 'Control Barrier Functions: Theory and Applications.' ECC 2019.
notes: The Ames 2017 paper is the most-cited modern reference; the Wieland 2007 paper is the deeper prior art origin.

disclosure_citation: Asimov, Isaac. Robots and Empire. Doubleday, 1985.
creator: Isaac Asimov
control_architecture: Adds 'A robot may not harm humanity, or, by inaction, allow humanity to come to harm' as priority-zero rule, restructuring the Three Laws priority order
notable_capabilities: tradeoff between individual harm and collective benefit
prior_art_notes: Significant for safety architecture prior art because it explicitly demonstrates priority-reordering in a hard-constraint hierarchy under conflicting goals. Anticipates modern AI safety frameworks dealing with population-scale or systemic harm tradeoffs.
notes: Pairs with the original Three Laws entry to provide a more complete picture of fictional priority-ordered safety architectures.

disclosure_citation: ISO 10218-1:2006 'Robots and robotic devices — Safety requirements for industrial robots — Part 1: Robots.' International Organization for Standardization.
creator: ISO TC 299 (Robotics) working group
control_architecture: Defines speed and separation monitoring, power and force limiting, hand guiding, safety-rated monitored stop
notable_capabilities: industry-standard safety modes for collaborative robots
categorical safety requirements for power-and-force-limited operation
prior_art_notes: ISO 10218 (and the related ISO/TS 15066 for collaborative operation) constitute foundational prior art for collaborative robot safety claims. Any patent claim around 'safety-rated monitored stop,' 'speed and separation monitoring,' or 'power and force limiting' in collaborative robotics is anticipated by these standards.
notes: Including standards documents in the corpus is a deliberate choice: they are publicly disclosed, dated, and constitute defensive prior art for claims in their domain.

disclosure_citation: Mitchell, I.M., Bayen, A.M., Tomlin, C.J. 'A time-dependent Hamilton-Jacobi formulation of reachable sets for continuous dynamic games.' IEEE TAC 50(7), 2005.
creator: Ian Mitchell, Alexandre Bayen, Claire Tomlin (UC Berkeley/Stanford)
control_architecture: Computes backward-reachable sets representing states from which a safety-violating state can be forced by adversary inputs; produces verified safe controllers
notable_capabilities: formally verified safety in continuous nonlinear systems
prior_art_notes: Foundational prior art for formally-verified safe control. Any patent claiming 'verified safety envelopes' or 'formal safety guarantees' for autonomous systems must contend with HJ reachability work.
sources: Mitchell, I.M. et al. IEEE TAC 50(7), 2005.
Bansal, S. et al. 'Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability: A Brief Overview and Recent Advances.' CDC 2017.
notes: Tomlin's group at UCB has been the most prolific source of HJ reachability applications.

disclosure_citation: Alshiekh, M. et al. 'Safe Reinforcement Learning via Shielding.' AAAI 2018.
creator: Mohammed Alshiekh, Roderick Bloem, Rüdiger Ehlers, Bettina Könighofer, Scott Niekum, Ufuk Topcu
control_architecture: Synthesized reactive shield monitors RL agent actions and overrides any action that could violate temporal-logic safety specification
notable_capabilities: formal safety guarantees during RL training and deployment
temporal logic specification of safety properties
prior_art_notes: Major prior art for any patent on RL safety filtering, shielded ML, or temporal-logic-bounded RL. Combined with Simplex and CBF prior art, makes much of the 'safe ML' patent space difficult to defend.
sources: Subsequent work by Könighofer, Bloem, others.
notes: Particularly relevant to physical AI deployment patents where ML-based control is wrapped in formal safety mechanisms.

disclosure_citation: Ogura, Y. et al. 'Development of a New Humanoid Robot WABIAN-2.' ICRA 2006.
creator: Waseda University, Takanishi Laboratory
notable_capabilities: designed as a human walking research platform
prior_art_notes: WABIAN-2's stretched-knee gait disclosure is significant prior art for any humanoid walking control claim aiming at more human-like locomotion (less crouched, more upright knees during stance). Distinct from ASIMO's bent-knee paradigm. The Takanishi laboratory's continued publication makes this a well-anchored academic disclosure.
notes: Continues the Waseda lineage from WABOT-1. WABIAN-2R is a refined variant.

disclosure_citation: Hirose, M. and Ogawa, K. 'Honda humanoid robots development.' Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 365, 11–19 (2007).
creator: Honda Motor Co.
control_architecture: static walking, faster cycle than E0
ip_citations: Honda program disclosed retrospectively in Hirose/Ogawa 2007 Phil Trans paper
prior_art_notes: Step in the Honda E-series lineage. Hirose/Ogawa 2007 documents the entire E0–E6 progression with sufficient specificity to anticipate basic electric-actuated bipedal walking claims for that era.
sources: Hirose, M. and Ogawa, K. Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 365, 11–19 (2007).
notes: Each E-series entry derives its primary disclosure from the same Hirose/Ogawa 2007 paper.

disclosure_citation: Hirose, M. and Ogawa, K. 'Honda humanoid robots development.' Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 365, 11–19 (2007).
creator: Honda Motor Co.
control_architecture: first dynamic walking in Honda lineage; Honda's first robot to walk at human-equivalent speed (1.2 km/h)
ip_citations: Hirose/Ogawa 2007 Phil Trans paper retrospective disclosure
prior_art_notes: E2 is the transition from static to dynamic walking in the Honda program. Disclosure relevant to dynamic bipedal walking claims.
sources: Hirose, M. and Ogawa, K. Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 365, 11–19 (2007).

disclosure_citation: Hirose, M. and Ogawa, K. 'Honda humanoid robots development.' Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 365, 11–19 (2007).
creator: Honda Motor Co.
prior_art_notes: Step in Honda E-series. Walking-speed progression relevant to bipedal locomotion speed claims.
sources: Hirose, M. and Ogawa, K. Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 365, 11–19 (2007).

disclosure_citation: Hirose, M. and Ogawa, K. 'Honda humanoid robots development.' Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 365, 11–19 (2007).
creator: Honda Motor Co.
notable_capabilities: walking at ~4.7 km/h with knee bending
prior_art_notes: Knee-bending dynamic walking variant in the Honda lineage.
sources: Hirose, M. and Ogawa, K. Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 365, 11–19 (2007).

disclosure_citation: Hirose, M. and Ogawa, K. 'Honda humanoid robots development.' Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 365, 11–19 (2007).
creator: Honda Motor Co.

sources: Hirose, M. and Ogawa, K. Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 365, 11–19 (2007).

disclosure_citation: Hirose, M. and Ogawa, K. 'Honda humanoid robots development.' Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 365, 11–19 (2007).
creator: Honda Motor Co.
actuator_details: Electric servos with active stair-climbing capability
prior_art_notes: Final E-series model before transition to P-series. Relevant to bipedal stair-climbing claims.
sources: Hirose, M. and Ogawa, K. Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 365, 11–19 (2007).

disclosure_citation: Hirose, M. and Ogawa, K. 'Honda humanoid robots development.' Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 365, 11–19 (2007).
creator: Honda Motor Co.
actuator_details: First Honda humanoid with arms in addition to legs
control_architecture: whole-body coordination, separate from previous legs-only platforms
notable_capabilities: first full-humanoid (legs + arms + torso) in Honda lineage
prior_art_notes: Transition from legs-only to full humanoid in the Honda lineage. P1 is the architectural ancestor of ASIMO. Anticipates subsequent claims around full-humanoid actuated platforms with arms and legs.
sources: Hirose, M. and Ogawa, K. Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 365, 11–19 (2007).
notes: P2 (1996) and P3 (1997) follow before ASIMO (2000); covered separately in next pass.

disclosure_citation: Honda Motor Co. press release, December 20, 1996, Tokyo. Hirose, M. and Ogawa, K. Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 365, 11–19 (2007).
creator: Honda Motor Co.
control_architecture: ZMP-based dynamic balancing; first published Honda ZMP work
notable_capabilities: public reveal shocked humanoid robotics community
ip_citations: Honda patents on bipedal control filed late 1990s; many now expired
prior_art_notes: P2's December 1996 reveal is among the most significant single events in humanoid robotics history. Honda's ZMP-based dynamic balancing as publicly disclosed via P2 anticipates virtually all subsequent commercial bipedal locomotion claims using ZMP. Honda's 1990s patent filings, many of which have now expired, form the deepest commercial prior art chain in the field.
sources: Hirose, M. and Ogawa, K. Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 365, 11–19 (2007).
Hirai, K. et al. 'The development of Honda humanoid robot.' ICRA 1998.
notes: Hirai et al. ICRA 1998 is the definitive academic disclosure of P2's design. Among the highest-value commons entries because it predates and anticipates so much.

disclosure_citation: Honda Motor Co. press materials, September 1997. Hirose, M. and Ogawa, K. Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 365, 11–19 (2007).
creator: Honda Motor Co.
actuator_details: Harmonic-drive electric servos; magnesium-alloy frame for weight reduction
notable_capabilities: lighter and more agile than P2
prior_art_notes: Final Honda P-series prototype before ASIMO. Refinements to the P2 architecture; key continuity in the Honda prior art chain.
sources: Hirose, M. and Ogawa, K. Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 365, 11–19 (2007).

disclosure_citation: Kaneko, K. et al. 'Humanoid Robot HRP-3.' IROS 2008.
creator: AIST and Kawada Industries
actuator_details: Harmonic-drive electric servos with dust/water resistance
prior_art_notes: HRP-3's environmental sealing disclosures anticipate subsequent IP-rated humanoid claims. The HRP series is a deep commons asset because of consistent open academic disclosure across generations.

disclosure_citation: Kaneko, K. et al. 'Humanoid Robot HRP-4: Humanoid Robotics Platform with Lightweight and Slim Body.' IROS 2010.

disclosure_citation: Kaneko, K. et al. 'Humanoid Robot HRP-5P: An Electrically Actuated Humanoid Robot With High-Power and Wide-Range Joints.' IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters 4(2), 2019.
creator: AIST and Kawada Industries
actuator_details: High-power harmonic-drive servos with wide range of motion
prior_art_notes: HRP-5P's construction-task demonstrations and high-power actuator disclosures are among the most thoroughly published examples of humanoid construction work. Anticipates many subsequent industrial humanoid claims.
sources: Kaneko, K. et al. IEEE RA-L 4(2), 2019.
notes: Continues the HRP series' uninterrupted open-academic disclosure tradition.

disclosure_citation: Figure AI public reveal of Figure 02, August 2024.
creator: Figure AI
actuator_details: Custom electric actuators; Figure-claimed 50% torque-density improvement over Figure 01
ip_citations: Figure patent filings; specifics largely undisclosed
prior_art_notes: Figure 02 actuator and hand claims are heavily anticipated by Honda P-series, Robonaut 2, Shadow Hand, and iCub work. The 16-DoF hand is in the same design space as Robonaut 2's 12-DoF and Sanctuary's 21-DoF.
sources: Figure AI website and demonstration videos.
notes: Figure has rapid product iteration; specifications change between announcements.

disclosure_citation: Hubicki, C. et al. 'ATRIAS: Design and validation of a tether-free 3D-capable spring-mass bipedal robot.' International Journal of Robotics Research 35(12), 2016.
creator: Oregon State University, Dynamic Robotics Laboratory (Jonathan Hurst)
actuator_details: Series-elastic actuators with fiberglass leaf-spring legs implementing the spring-loaded inverted pendulum (SLIP) model
notable_capabilities: first machine to walk in 3D space using passive-dynamics-inspired control
demonstrated robust unscripted human-like walking gaits
ip_citations: academic publication; OSU patents licensed widely
prior_art_notes: ATRIAS is foundational prior art for spring-mass bipedal locomotion. The SLIP-based reduced-order control approach has become a dominant paradigm in dynamic bipedal walking, anticipating many subsequent commercial control claims.
sources: Hurst, J. et al. various IROS and ICRA publications, 2012-2015.
notes: Direct ancestor of Cassie which became the basis for Agility Robotics' Digit. The Hurst-lab academic chain is among the most-cited in modern bipedal robotics.

disclosure_citation: Park, H.-W. et al. 'High-speed bounding with the MIT Cheetah 2: Control design and experiments.' International Journal of Robotics Research 36(2), 2017. Earlier ICRA disclosure 2014.
creator: MIT Biomimetic Robotics Lab (Sangbae Kim)
ip_citations: MIT academic publications; Wensing 2017 T-RO paper on actuator design
prior_art_notes: MIT Cheetah 2 establishes the QDD actuator topology in a working high-speed legged robot. The Wensing 2017 T-RO paper 'Proprioceptive actuator design in the MIT Cheetah' is the foundational actuator design disclosure.
sources: Wensing, P.M. et al. 'Proprioceptive actuator design in the MIT Cheetah.' IEEE T-RO 33(3), 2017.
notes: Original MIT Cheetah (1) was hydraulic; Cheetah 2 transitioned to electric QDD which became the architectural standard.

disclosure_citation: Bledt, G. et al. 'MIT Cheetah 3: Design and Control of a Robust, Dynamic Quadruped Robot.' IROS 2018.
creator: MIT Biomimetic Robotics Lab (Sangbae Kim)
prior_art_notes: Cheetah 3 establishes blind robust legged locomotion using only proprioceptive sensing — a significant prior art point against later vision-dependent legged-robot claims.
notes: Cheetah 3 was directly downscaled into the Mini Cheetah platform.

disclosure_citation: Unitree Robotics Go1 reveal, June 2021.
creator: Unitree Robotics
actuator_details: Custom QDD actuators, derived from MIT Cheetah-style design
ip_citations: Unitree patent filings primarily in PRC
prior_art_notes: Unitree Go1 actuator design is heavily anticipated by MIT Cheetah QDD prior art (Wensing 2017, Katz 2019). Pricing-driven commodification rather than novel IP.
notes: Go1 is the most-deployed Unitree platform and the immediate predecessor to the H1 humanoid architecture.

disclosure_citation: Yokoyama, Mitsuteru. Tetsujin 28-go, serialized in Shōnen magazine, beginning July 1956.
creator: Mitsuteru Yokoyama
actuator_details: Pre-WWII-developed giant humanoid weapon platform; remote-controlled by handheld console
control_architecture: radio-controlled by external operator (key thematic element)
notable_capabilities: piloted by external remote control rather than internal cockpit
prior_art_notes: Foundational fictional disclosure of giant humanoid robot. Establishes the mecha morphology that influences the entire subsequent Japanese robot fiction tradition. The remote-control rather than piloted-cockpit architecture is a notable structural distinction from later mecha (Mazinger, Gundam) where the operator is inside.
notes: Predates Mazinger Z (1972) by 16 years and is the deeper root of the Japanese mecha tradition.

disclosure_citation: AgiBot (Shanghai Zhiyuan New Technology) public reveal, August 2023.

disclosure_citation: Brohan, A. et al. 'RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control.' arXiv 2307.15818, July 2023.
creator: Google DeepMind
control_architecture: VLA model leveraging vision-language pretraining for manipulation
notable_capabilities: transfer of web-pretrained knowledge to manipulation
prior_art_notes: RT-2 is foundational publicly-disclosed prior art for VLA architectures applied to robotics. Any subsequent VLA patent claim must contend with this disclosure.
notes: DeepMind has published the RT-1, RT-2, and RT-X series openly via arXiv, making them strong commons assets.

disclosure_citation: Open X-Embodiment Collaboration. 'Open X-Embodiment: Robotic Learning Datasets and RT-X Models.' arXiv 2310.08864, October 2023.
creator: 34-lab international collaboration coordinated by Google DeepMind
control_architecture: cross-embodiment learning from heterogeneous robot data
notable_capabilities: largest unified robot manipulation dataset (~1M episodes)
ip_citations: arXiv preprint and dataset releases under Apache 2.0
prior_art_notes: Open X-Embodiment is the dominant publicly-disclosed prior art for cross-embodiment learning. The dataset itself plus the architectural paper anticipate broad swaths of cross-platform manipulation foundation model claims.
notes: Critically important commons asset; 34 labs participating creates broad prior art base.

prior_art_notes: Hanson's Frubber synthetic skin material and facial actuation prior art is significant for any claim around expressive humanoid faces. Disney Imagineering's earlier work is the deeper prior art.
